Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

know verb

a fact; how to

also know how to, I don’t know, as far as I know, know for sure, know for certain, I know for a fact

classical

Varr. RR 2.1.2: nēmō enim omnia potest scīre
Liv. 22.51.4: vincere scīs, Hannibal
Traupman 30

sciō, scīre, scīvī, scītum

verb, fourth conjugation

know (a fact); know how to (with an infinitive)

Facts: with an object, an accusative and infinitive, or an indirect question (scīre quid agās). With an infinitive, know how to (vincere scīs); of a language, scīre Latīnē (Cic. Brut. 140, Lewis & Short). Quod sciam, as far as I know (Cic. Att. 16.2.4). People and places one knows take nōvī instead.

Other words

  • nesciō, nescīre, nescīvī, nescītum — not know; Nesciō, I don’t know

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Catull. 85.2: nesciō, sed fierī sentiō; Traupman 30

    The ordinary way to say it: nōn scīre is rare, and Cicero says it already sounds barbarous beside nescīre (Or. 157, cited by Lewis & Short).

  • certiōrem facere — let someone know, inform

    phrase: the person informed in the accusative; dē and the ablative, an accusative and infinitive, or an indirect question · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 3.11.1: faciam tē certiōrem quid ēgerim; Traupman 102

    The prose way to say “inform” (Lewis & Short, s.v. certus). In a letter, “let me know” is fac sciam or fac ut sciam.

  • certō sciō — I know for sure

    the adverb certō with sciō · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.19: fīliolam tuam et amō et amābilem esse certō sciō (Lewis & Short), s.v. amābilis; Ter. Eun. 5.2.50: volet, certō sciō (Lewis & Short), s.v. ah; Traupman 102: certum (certō) sciō

Examples

  • nēmō enim omnia potest scīre

    for nobody can know everythingVarr. RR 2.1.2

  • vincere scīs, Hannibal; victōriā ūtī nescīs

    you know how to win, Hannibal; you don’t know how to use a victoryLiv. 22.51.4

  • fac sciam quid agās

    let me know how you arePlin. Ep. 1.11.2

  • nūllae, quod sciam

    none, as far as I knowCic. Off. 3.59

  • pater, quī Bulgaricē nōn minus quam Latīnē scit

    Dad, who knows Bulgarian no less than LatinLibellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

See also know, sure, ask, learn.
